hanging-tie.chosenBody: Cord only, with its own weight negligible in the explicitly stated introductory model.
hanging-tie.externalForces: Load/platform interaction pulls downward on the cord; support pulls upward at its other end.
hanging-tie.effects: At rest, the whole cord has balanced external forces; those loads can stretch the cord and are related to the internal tension, not identical to it.
hanging-tie.changedCase: Draw the same chosen member in a changed orientation or with a changed supplied load/support interaction. Identify the outside interactions acting ON it; if the member’s own weight is no longer negligible include its weight as another external force. Use given magnitudes/relative arrows only, not invented measured newtons.
hanging-tie.limit: This is a bounded original model; chosen-body force balance, shape response and internal loading are distinct accounts. No construction safety limit or load capacity is inferred.

supporting-column.chosenBody: Foam column only, with its own weight negligible in the explicitly stated introductory model.
supporting-column.externalForces: Platform pushes down on the column; base pushes up on the column.
supporting-column.effects: Whole-body rest can coexist with squeezing/deformation. A column can resist its supplied small load; visible non-motion does not show no forces.

sagging-beam.chosenBody: Foam beam only, with its own weight negligible in the explicitly stated introductory model.
sagging-beam.externalForces: Central applied load pushes down on the beam; the two supports push up on it.
sagging-beam.effects: The beam bends downward under the stated loading even though its overall support/load balance holds. Do not infer no external force or no deformation from rest.

actions: Actually identify the chosen member and the external load/support interactions in all three prepared cases. Distinguish a force on this member from a force it exerts on another object and from its internal tension/compression.

Produce and interpret member force diagrams: arrows start on the chosen body, direction is the direction of force and length means supplied relative magnitude. A supported resting member must not be drawn with no forces. Use equal total upwards/downwards loading in the stated balanced models; the two beam supports together balance the central load, neither alone is assumed to equal it.

Explain the actual structural effects: stretching a cord, squeezing a column, bending the beam. A stationary whole structure can deform; relate supplied contact load/support to shape response and treat a real member’s gravitational weight as external when not negligible.

Transfer to the changed orientation/added-load case, distinguishing contact from gravitational interaction without requiring an irrelevant magnetic demonstration. Report uncertainty when load/support details are missing.
